[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Matilda Glasgow was born in Ireland on 30 March 1826. She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-1675|William Glasgow]] and [[Glendinning-340|Nancy Glendinning]]. She married [[Ewing-2680|James Ewing Jr.]] on 22 December 1854 in Sandusky, Erie County, Ohio.

Her gravestone records that she died on 2 July 1898. An obituary image on the same memorial independently gives the same date.<ref name="FAG131676817">{{FindAGrave|131676817|sameas=no}}; the memorial includes photographs of the gravestone and an obituary.</ref>

Recorded residences:
* 1860: Taylor Creek Township, Hardin County, Ohio
* 1870: Kenton, Pleasant Township, Hardin County, Ohio
* 1880: Taylor Creek Township, Hardin County, Ohio


The unsigned 1903 <i>A Brief Memorial of the Deceased Members of the Glendinning Family</i>, under “Glasgow–Glendinning Family,” describes Nancy as the elder’s fifth daughter, born in April 1803, whose mother was Mary Bell. It says [[Glendinning-340|Nancy]] married [[Glasgow-1675|William Glasgow]] of Killycorragh and names five sons—[[Glasgow-3148|Henry Cunningham]], Adam, [[Glasgow-3149|Isaac Watts]], [[Glasgow-3150|Benjamin]] and [[Glasgow-2825|Alexander Flemming]]—and three daughters—[[Glasgow-3158|Mary]], [[Glasgow-3146|Matilda]] and [[Glasgow-3147|Jane]]. It records Nancy’s death at Belle Center on 20 March 1890, aged 87. The passage supplies no father or other kin for William.<ref name="Glendinning1903">Unsigned, <i>A Brief Memorial of the Deceased Members of the Glendinning Family</i> (1903), “Glasgow–Glendinning Family,” PDF page 17 (no printed page number), [https://glendinning.name/history/irish_glendinning.pdf#page=17 original booklet]; page and 1903 cover visually checked 24 October 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Father and family identification ===

The relationship to [[Glasgow-1675|William Glasgow]] is assessed at 92% (confident). The named daughter Matilda fits the Irish-born woman who married James Ewing in Sandusky on 22 December 1854, a specific place and family setting matching William’s Sandusky association before his 1855 death. Her stone and obituary independently support her dates, not a quoted parent clause; the full adult identification remains an inference. The booklet explicitly names the children, but each identification with a later adult must be assessed separately. The WikiTree Space account of this booklet is derivative of the same family tradition, not a second independent witness. This assessment concerns the paternal link; it does not establish further ancestry for William or resolve every maternal or vital detail.
